title: private-installer: terraform lifecycle module + helm & installer hooks for rollback-safe audit export sinks
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Add terraform module for managed audit export sink lifecycle, helm values/crd to enforce retention, and installer upgrade/rollback hooks to ensure sinks are validated and cleaned up safely.
description:
Context: Private deployments need audited export sinks (S3/GCS) for compliance. Existing installer created sinks on first install but lacked lifecycle management and produced risk during upgrades/rollbacks when sink state diverged from installer expectations. This PR introduces a coordinated terraform module, helm-side retention enforcement, and installer hooks to make audit-sink lifecycle safe and idempotent across upgrades and rollback scenarios.

What this PR does: Adds a new terraform module (terraform/modules/audit_sink) which: creates a tenant-scoped export sink (S3/GCS), attaches explicit IAM/service-account roles, and wires lifecycle blocks (prevent_destroy toggles and separate retention policy resource). The module emits a stable sink_id used by the private control plane. Adds a --sink-provisioned flag so the installer can opt-out if upstream resource ownership is external.

Installer/Helm changes: Adds installer pre-upgrade validation hook (installer/hooks/validate-audit-sink.sh) which runs a sink preflight check via the private control plane API and ensures retention meets org policy. Adds a post-install/upgrade hook (installer/hooks/ensure-audit-annotations.go) which writes current sink metadata into a ConfigMap consumed by the audit-log-exporter helm chart. The helm chart (helm-charts/private/templates/audit-exporter.yaml) now supports a retentionEnforcement CRD and a values.schema.json flag to validate retention ranges at install time.

Rollback safety: Introduces a rollback-safe pattern by separating sink lifecycle from the control plane resource reference. The terraform module uses prevent_destroy=false by default but exposes a 'prevent_destroy' boolean and 'ownership' enum (installer|external) so customers can pin ownership during migration. Installer upgrade hooks will not delete sinks; instead, on detects of a failed upgrade the post-rollback hook (installer/rollback/cleanup-audit-hooks.go) re-applies the ConfigMap state and triggers a no-op reconciliation path in audit-log-exporter.

Migration & cleanup: Includes a migration script (scripts/migrate_sinks_to_tf.py) to adopt existing installer-created sinks into the new terraform-managed state by normalizing names and annotating buckets with a shard-id label. Also adds an idempotent S3 multipart cleanup job (scripts/s3_multipart_cleanup.sh) to reduce storage leakage for older buckets that were previously orphaned.

Testing and CI: Adds e2e tests (tests/e2e/audit_sink_lifecycle_test.go) that run against a local kind cluster with a mocked S3 backend. Adds a nightly pipeline job 'private/audit-sink-lifecycle' to exercise upgrades and rollbacks against the module.

Motivation: This reduces on-call churn from incidents where upgrades inadvertently removed or orphaned export sinks, and enforces retention policies required by compliance teams (SOC2). It also enables enterprise customers to adopt terraform-managed sinks or keep external ownership without losing installer automation.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing default ownership to terraform to reduce blast radius; the default remains installer-managed but opt-in migration is documented. See docs/private/audit-sink-terraform.md for migration steps.

merge_outcome: merged via squash merge. Commit message consolidated. Post-merge actions: created a follow-up issue ENG-10021 to track GA rollout and telemetry, kicked off nightly pipeline and announced migration docs to customer-facing install guide.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: default ownership remains installer to avoid surprising existing private deployments.
Operators who want full terraform control should set module.ownership="terraform" and follow docs/private/audit-sink-terraform.md migration steps.
Migration is best-effort; customers with encrypted buckets should coordinate with support (SUP-5432) before adopting.
Follow-up work: add HSM/KMS key rotation integration for bucket server-side encryption (ENG-10022).
